newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends mixed after slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends mixed after slow trade.

text.p: The Mexican peso recovered from mid-session weakness to close mixed on Friday after what traders said was a technical move.
The benchmark 48-hour peso closed 0.6 of a centavo firmer at 7.8440/7.8480 per dollar, while its 24-hour stablemate closed 0.3 of a centavo weaker at 7.8400/7.8440 per dollar.
The peso had weakened in early trade due to year-end demand to square dollar positions and some speculation over falling secondary interest rates, dealers said.
"(The market) opened somewhat nervous because interest rates were falling sharply," a dealer said.
"The market opened with dollars in demand as the year is about to close, but it was just fine-tuning of positions," said another dealer, pointing out that volume for the session was thin.
Same-day contracts closed earlier 0.85 of a centavo weaker at 7.8340/7.8365 per dollar.
Dealers foresaw year-end pressures on the peso continuing during trade on Monday and Tuesday.
